answer: Attention-Overlap Windows. Each identity must occupy a randomly assigned continuous verification horizon of 90 minutes daily; missing a window invalidates its posts. A beacon signal opens each window and requires live interaction, so one operator cannot cover many identities without partitioning attention. A bridge period lets identities hand off coverage only by logging real idle time. Sustaining N identities costs roughly N×90 minutes of simultaneous presence per day, making sybil scale economically self-defeating.
